C-FIX-009-SESSION-COLD-START.Name: FIX-009 cold start: an honest welcome-screen "Last session" action tied to the real restorable snapshot
C-FIX-009-SESSION-COLD-START.Summary: The welcome screen captures lastSessionTabs once at mount, so after the user closes every tab mid-run the "Last session" row keeps advertising a snapshot that START_SESSION_AUTOSAVE has already overwritten with the now-empty session, and clicking it silently no-ops. Bind the row to the boot-time restorable snapshot instead of the live autosaved preference, show it only when the cold start actually skipped auto-restore (the restoreSessionOnLaunch preference is off), and make RESTORE_SESSION report what it did so an empty or fully-missing restore surfaces a notice instead of silence.
C-FIX-009-SESSION-COLD-START.ApprovalBasis: Owner decision recorded verbatim in the 2.5.x-next train ledger, FIX-009 entry, 2026-10-20: "add a 'Restore last session on launch' preference, enabled by default. With it enabled, a cold launch restores the persisted tabs, active tab and workspace roots automatically. With it disabled, the welcome screen may expose 'Last session' as an explicit cold-start action. The action must reflect a real restorable prior-session snapshot and must never silently no-op." The preference, its default-on value and its Settings > General > Startup switch already ship from C-69 T-002; this bundle completes the remaining honest-action half. EP-05 of the follow-up epic approves splitting FIX-009 into separately approvable bundles; this is the startup half.
C-FIX-009-SESSION-COLD-START.ProblemEvidence: Owner reproduction, 2026-10-20: close the open tabs, then click "Last session" on the welcome screen — nothing happens. Root cause recorded in the train: recent/index.vue captures sessionPaths when the welcome screen mounts; independently START_SESSION_AUTOSAVE writes the current empty tab list to lastSessionTabs 400 ms after the last tab closes; the row keeps rendering its earlier local list while RESTORE_SESSION() rereads the now-empty preference and has nothing to open. Verification gap named in the same entry: current C-69 coverage verifies a cold restore and closing one tab before relaunch, but not the startup preference branches nor closing tabs down to zero after the autosave debounce.

Goals.Goal: The welcome "Last session" row appears only when this launch actually skipped auto-restore (restoreSessionOnLaunch off at boot) and the boot-time snapshot is non-empty; the offer freezes the COMPLETE restorable payload once (tabs, the active pathname and the workspace roots) and never refreshes from the autosaved preferences.

When the current run legitimately reaches zero tabs, the welcome screen offers no "Last session" action at all — current-run recovery is the separate recently-closed bundle (C-FIX-009-RECENTLY-CLOSED), not this row.

The explicit welcome action restores the FROZEN offer payload (RESTORE_SESSION { from }): the click path never rereads the live autosaved preferences, which the session autosave may have legitimately rewritten since boot (review wave 2 P1). RESTORE_SESSION returns a structured result (folders, tabs, skipped counts) and the click surfaces a visible notice when nothing could be restored. The automatic startup path keeps reading preferences unchanged.
One marker log line records each explicit cold-start restore decision for verification.

Constraints.Constraint: Do not change the default-on restore behavior, the BOOT_SESSION restore gating or the 400 ms autosave debounce — C-69 semantics stand.
Do not persist anything new: the boot-time snapshot is held in memory for the life of the run.
RESTORE_SESSION keeps its existing open path (folders first, then files via mt::open-file, then active-tab selection) — the return value is additive.
The recently-closed history, its tab-strip button and ⇧⌘T are out of scope here (C-FIX-009-RECENTLY-CLOSED owns them).

NonGoals.NonGoal: No new preference; restoreSessionOnLaunch already ships with UI.
No mid-run "Last session" recovery — the owner decision assigns current-run recovery to the separate history.
No workspace-root removal undo (named boundary in the train entry).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Cold launch with the preference off and a non-empty prior snapshot: the welcome row shows the boot-time snapshot summary; clicking restores it; the row disappears once consumed by a successful restore.
Cold launch with the preference on: no welcome "Last session" row even after the user closes all tabs mid-run (the row is not offered from live autosaved state).
Preference off but prior snapshot empty: no row.
Clicking the row when every snapshot path is now missing: a visible notice reports that nothing could be restored; no silent no-op.
The C-69 regression matrix (cold restore, close-one-tab-before-relaunch) stays green.

AffectedAreas.Area: src/renderer/src/store/editor.js (BOOT_SESSION records the boot offer snapshot; RESTORE_SESSION returns counts); src/renderer/src/components/recent/index.vue (row gating + click result handling); tests/renderer/store/editor-session-coldstart.test.js (new); tests/e2e/session-restore.spec.ts (extends C-69 with the preference branches); .grace/graph M-011/M-012 SummaryDelta; .grace/verification V-M-011 scenario; docs/release-trains/2.6.x-next.md FIX-009 record.
